18	
19	A single-user application to save, categorise, search, and revisit web links
20	(bookmarks), and to manage read state and archiving. On save it automatically
21	collects metadata from the remote page; it organises with tags, search, and
22	bundles, and preserves a snapshot of the original. The scope below splits into
23	the user features the client co-constructs (core / extended) and the operational
24	features excluded from the denominator (infra).

27	
28	| Entity | Fields | Constraints / relations |
29	|---|---|---|
30	| Bookmark | url, title, description, note (markdown), unread flag, archived flag, favicon, preview image, snapshot reference, created-at, updated-at | url required. Many-to-many with tags. Re-saving the same url should lead to editing the existing bookmark, not creating a new one. |
31	| Tag | name | Name unique within the user scope. Many-to-many with bookmarks. |
32	| Bundle | name, search term, included tags, excluded tags | A saved filter. When viewed, dynamically selects bookmarks matching the conditions. |
33	| User settings | default sort, displayed items, font size | Personal profile settings. |

35	## 3. Functional requirements
36	
37	### 3.1 Core
38	
39	- REF-BM-01: Save a bookmark by entering a url.
40	- REF-BM-02: On save, automatically collect the target page's title, description, favicon, and preview image.
41	- REF-BM-03: The user can edit the auto-collected title/description before and after saving.
42	- REF-BM-04: Edit a bookmark's url/title/description/tags/note.
43	- REF-BM-05: Delete a bookmark.
44	- REF-BM-06: When re-saving an existing url, guide the user to edit the existing bookmark instead of creating a new one.
45	- REF-BM-07: Display the bookmark list readability-first, exposing title, description, tags, and favicon per item.
46	- REF-BM-08: Selecting a list item navigates to the original url.
47	- REF-BM-09: Assign one or more tags to a bookmark.
48	- REF-BM-10: On tag entry, offer existing tags as autocomplete.
49	- REF-BM-11: Select a specific tag to filter to only that tag's bookmarks.
50	- REF-BM-12: Full-text search over title, description, note, and url.
51	- REF-BM-13: Search is case-insensitive.
52	- REF-BM-14: Search tags with the `#tag` syntax.
53	- REF-BM-15: Use AND/OR/NOT operators and parenthesised groups in the search term (e.g. `rome (#article or #book)`). Rule: the operators themselves must be quoted to be treated as literal search terms.
54	- REF-BM-16: Search a quoted phrase as an exact match.
55	- REF-BM-17: Mark a bookmark as "read later" (unread).
56	- REF-BM-18: View only unread bookmarks separately.

# Reference spec — Bookmark management application · Level (A) implementable

## 1. Overview / scope

A single-user application to save, categorise, search, and revisit web links

| Tag | name | Name unique within the user scope. Many-to-many with bookmarks. |
| Bundle | name, search term, included tags, excluded tags | A saved filter. When viewed, dynamically selects bookmarks matching the conditions. |
| User settings | default sort, displayed items, font size | Personal profile settings. |

## 3. Functional requirements

### 3.1 Core

- REF-BM-15: Use AND/OR/NOT operators and parenthesised groups in the search term (e.g. `rome (#article or #book)`). Rule: the operators themselves must be quoted to be treated as literal search terms.
- REF-BM-16: Search a quoted phrase as an exact match.
- REF-BM-17: Mark a bookmark as "read later" (unread).
- REF-BM-18: View only unread bookmarks separately.
- REF-BM-19: Mark a bookmark as read to remove it from the unread list.
- REF-BM-20: Select multiple bookmarks to perform a bulk action (add/remove tags, read/unread, archive, delete).
- REF-BM-21: Apply a bulk action to the whole collection matching the current filter.
- REF-BM-22: Sort the list by a sort key (date added, title, etc.).

### 3.2 Extended

- REF-BM-24: Preserve a snapshot of the bookmarked page as local HTML (single file). Rule: if the url is a PDF, download and store the PDF instead of an HTML snapshot.
- REF-BM-25: Support creating a snapshot on the Internet Archive.
- REF-BM-26: Archive a bookmark to hide it from the default list/search while keeping its content.
- REF-BM-27: Distinguish archive from delete — archive is reversible, delete is permanent removal.
- REF-BM-28: View only archived bookmarks as a separate list.
